extensions.reason:
1) Delay of 2 years in receiving High Rise Committee (HRC) NOC from TMC. When the project was launched, there was no HRC in place in Thane. In the midst of the project, HRC was instituted in Thane and our Commencement Certificate (CC) was reduced from 30 floors to 22 floors and we were told to apply for HRC to build more than 22 floors. And it took 1.5 years to get this HRC, a timeline we had absolutely not budgeted for when we applied for RERA.
2)Huge increase in costs of basic materials like Steel, Aluminium, glass, paint, electrical cables, tiles etc. due to increase in prices of fuel, gas and raw materials. Our project costs increased by a huge amount, and we had to gather huge funding in order to finish the project.
3) Delay in receipt of materials like soil, cement, admixtures, siporex blocks, admixtures, waterproofing chemical due to high demand and short supply of raw materials in the market (even after advance payment was made)
Considering the above points, completion of the project by 30th June 2023, as disclosed at the time of registration of the project, would be difficult to achieve.
In view of the aforesaid facts, we request you to kindly give us an extension of 1 year u/s 6 of Real Estate Act 2016 and grant us permission to revise the date of completion of the said Real Estate project to 29th June 2024 on RERA Website.

P51700000507.promoter_name: MATRIX ENCLAVES PROJECTS DEV. PVT. LTD

extensions.reason:
1)Delay of 2 years in receiving High Rise Committee (HRC) NOC from TMC. When the project was launched, there was no HRC in place in Thane. In the midst of the project, HRC was instituted in Thane and our Commencement Certificate (CC) was reduced from 30 floors to 22 floors and we were told to apply for HRC to build more than 22 floors. And it took 1.5 years to get this HRC, a timeline we had absolutely not budgeted for when we applied for RERA.
2)Huge increase in costs of basic materials like Steel, Aluminium, glass, paint, electrical cables, tiles etc. due to increase in prices of fuel, gas and raw materials. Our project costs increased by a huge amount, and we had to gather huge funding in order to finish the project.
3)Delay in receipt of materials like soil, cement, admixtures, siporex blocks, admixtures, waterproofing chemical due to high demand and short supply of raw materials in the market (even after advance payment was made)
Considering the above points, completion of the project by 30th June 2023, as disclosed at the time of registration of the project, would be difficult to achieve.
In view of the aforesaid facts, we request you to kindly give us an extension of 1 year u/s 6 of Real Estate Act 2016 and grant us permission to revise the date of completion of the said Real Estate project to 29th June 2024 on RERA Website.

extensions.reason:
1. DELAY DUE TO GOVT. ORDERS:
Environment Clearance Application was made on 20/11/2018 (construction of 26th Flr. to 35th Fl.) and permission was granted on 15/1/2020 (13 months delay).
Letter dtd. 18/5/2020 by Conservator of Forest and Dir. Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) To Principal Secretary Urban Devp. Dept. leading to such as ‘stop work’ notices, withholding of certificates by Municipal Corporations. Accordingly Principal Secretary of Environment Department issued Letter dtd. 30/6/2020 to Commissioner, TMC.
TMC by letters dtd. 23/9/2020, 11/11/2020 and 6/5/2021 sought guidance from Urban Dev. Dept. Mantralaya, for finalization of boundary for Eco-sensitive Zone on 11/9/2020.
Our Letter dtd. 25/5/2021 (28/5/2021) intimating TMC about Plinth completion of Podium of Building No. 1, wing A & B. TMC by Letter dtd. 29/6/2021 refused to process application.
Writ Petition No. 4725/2021 was filed before High Court, Mumbai on 4/8/2021 to quash/set aside the communication/ letter dated 18/02/2020, was allowed on 5/5/2022.
On account of the aforesaid there was delay from 18/5/2020 to 5/5/2022, (2 years)
b. Order of Supreme Court dtd. 3/6/2022 in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 202/1995) giving direction not to carry construction within 1 km (Eco-Sensitive Zone) and order dtd. 23/9/2022 holding that restriction is not be applicable to SGNP and Thane Flamingo Creek Sanctuary. (Delay 3 months)
2. DELAY FOR AMENDED PERMISSION/C.C.
The process of obtaining permission for construction from 26th Floor to 35th Floors had actually started on 20/11/2018 and concluded on 12/10/2022 – (4 Years).  The plans thereafter were revised and accordingly amended CC issued by TMC on 12/10/2022 and 26/02/2024.

P51700000528.project_name: MY CITY - PHASE I - PART I

extensions.reason:
We, have  registered  our project “My City - Phase I – Part I ” (hereinafter referred to as the said Project) on the RERA Website bearing Registration No.51700000528  on 18th July 2017. The “Revised Proposed Date of Completion” while registering the said Project was mentioned on RERA Website as 31/12/2020 for the completion of the Project and further it was sou moto extended by RERA Authority for 6 (six) months i.e. till 30/06/2021 due to lockdown declared by Maharashtra Government due to Covid-19.
We have completed the construction and the finishing work of the said Project and obtained Part Occupancy Certificate dated 9/3/2020. Now we are in process of applying for full Occupancy  Certificate in respect of the  said Project. 
We submit that we have acted diligently and have completed the construction work of the Project in time and the extension is being sought only to obtain the full Occupation Certificate which is the last step to complete the Project.  No prejudice will be caused if the extension as requested is granted.  We are committed to complying with our commitments to our customers and also committed to compliance with our statutory obligations under Real Estate Regulation Act and Rules framed thereunder. 
In view of the aforesaid it is humbly prayed that the extension till 30 June 2022  for the Revised Proposed Date of Completion date be granted.

extensions.reason: This is with reference to our project Mohan Areca, comprises of four wings A to D, bearing RERA Registration number P51700000829. The original date of completion of the project was proposed at 31st December 2019. However due to some uncontrolled reasons such as non-availability of some contractors and their laborers on time and also irregular/short supply of water caused delay in completion of project. Hence we are filing this application for project extension. Kindly accept our application and oblige.

This is with reference to our project Mohan Areca, bearing RERA Registration number P51700000829. 
The construction of project Mohan Areca was expected to be completed by December 2020.  However due to an unprecedented challenge in form of pandemic Covid-19, the construction activity of project is adversely affected.
In last year, the construction activity of the project halted for 4-5 months as per the government lockdown regulations.  Even after the relaxation of lockdown, the construction activity could not be started fully due to migration of labour and irregular supply of material. 
We were able to take-up regular construction speed in the month of November 2020 only, however again in the month of February 2021, Covid-19 second wave has started and all labour started moving to their native place. 
Further from 5th April 2021, lockdown like restrictions were imposed by the government caused difficulty in procuring material from local market and travelling of labour as well. From last 4 months, there is very limited availability of labour and supply of material. This has resulted in almost no construction activity in last 3-4 months.
Further, the cash flow is very important part for smooth functioning of any business. This pandemic has adversely impacted the income of many employees and businessmen. This has resulted in low new bookings and slow collection from existing customers. 
We appreciate that the government has given extension of 6 months last year. But the impact of Covid-19 last year and second wave this year is very huge and require further extension in timelines to complete the projects. 
Hence in view of unprecedented events, we request you to kindly accept our application and extend the project completion date to 30th June 2022.

extensions.reason:
We, have  registered  our project “Runwal Pearl” (hereinafter referred to as “the said Project”) on the RERA Website bearing Registration No.51700001383 on 27th July 2017. The “Revised Proposed Date of Completion” while registering the said Project was mentioned on RERA Website as 31/05/2019 for the completion of the project.
We hereby submit that the said Project registered under RERA consists of two towers namely Tower “A” (Doris) and Tower “E”  (Rissoina).  We further submit that we acted diligently and have completed the entire construction work of the  Tower “E” and obtained the Occupation Certificate dated 12th March 2018 for the said Tower “E” of the said Project. We have also completed major construction work of Tower “A” and obtained Part Occupation Certificate dated 9th April 2019 for said Tower “A” said Project. 
On receipt of Occupancy Certificates, we have offered possession to the customers of both the Towers. The said Occupation Certificates have been uploaded on RERA Website.
We hereby confirm that we shall endeavor to obtain the full Occupation Certificate of the said Project on or before 30th May 2020.  We, therefore, are making the present application for extension of the Date of Completion of the said Project for further period of 12 (Twelve) months i.e. till 30th May 2020. 
We submit no prejudice will be caused if the extension as requested is granted.  We are committed to complying with our commitments to our customers and also committed to compliance with our statutory obligations under Real Estate Regulation Act and Rules framed thereunder. 
In view of the aforesaid it is humbly prayed that the extension till 30th May 2020 for the Revised Proposed Date of Completion be granted.

The Tower E is granted full occupation certificate bearing number TMC/TDD/ OCC/0471/ 18 dated 12/03/2018 and the said tower E is fit for occupancy. However, Tower A is granted part OC bearing no.TMC/TDD/OCC/0681/19 dated 9th April 2019 and full occupancy certificate is awaited.

The Project Completion Date of the said Project mentioned on the RERA website was 31/12/2023.
We hereby state that, we have duly completed the construction of the building in the said Project as uploaded on RERA and received the Part Occupation Certificate dated  9th April 2019  and have uploaded the same on the RERA website.
We hereby state that, since there was delay in obtaining full occupation certificate, we have applied for the Certificate for Extension of Registration of Project under the provisions of RERA and the Authority has granted the extension for completion of said Project for the further period of 12 month i.e till 31/12/2023.  
We further state that, we have received the occupancy certificate for all the flats/units we have sold as on date and the same are in habitable condition, therefore no prejudice will cause to any customer due to delay in getting full occupancy certificate for the said Project. We further state and confirm that, we have not sold or created any third party interest in the flats/unit which are pending for receipt of occupancy certificate. 
 We further state that, we have also handed over the possession of the flats/units in the said Project to our registered customers and they have started residing there.
In view of the aforesaid it is humbly prayed that a short extension till 31st December 2024 be granted.
Occupancy Certificate is under Process, awaiting OC to receive

extensions.reason:
Reason for Delay & Extension Request

The completion of our registered project “Shree Haven” (Registration No. P51700002002) has been delayed due to a combination of unavoidable factors beyond our reasonable control, which have impacted the pace of construction and finishing works. The primary reasons include:

Pandemic Impact & Labour Shortage: COVID-19 restrictions and subsequent waves during and after 2020–2022 caused prolonged site work stoppages, slowed material supply, and labour migration, affecting critical construction milestones.

Approval & Regulatory Delays: Clearances for certain statutory works, including fire NOC, water connection, and electrical installations, took longer than expected due to procedural delays at relevant authorities.

Material Price Fluctuations & Supply Chain Disruptions: Unprecedented increases in cement, steel, and other raw material costs along with irregular supply in the past two years hampered procurement schedules.

Unseasonal Rains & Weather Impact: Prolonged and unpredictable rainfall over consecutive years affected structural and finishing activity timelines, particularly waterproofing, external plaster, and site development works.

Coordination for Service & Amenity Installations: Synchronising multiple agencies for lifts, fire-fighting equipment, STP, rainwater harvesting, and landscaping required additional time, especially with imported equipment procurement timelines.

Extension Period Justification

As per the revised PERT Chart & project schedule, completion of all structural, finishing, service, and external works is targeted for December 2027. This includes time for:

Finishing & internal works – by March 2026

Interior/Services installation – by March 2027

External development & site works – by December 2027

We are also including a buffer period for obtaining Occupancy Certificate (OC), which typically requires 3–6 months after physical completion for inspections, rectifications, and final clearances from various departments.

Therefore, the requested extension period up to 31/12/2027 ensures not only the completion of all physical work but also covers the statutory approval phase for OC, so that possession can be offered in a compliant manner.

There was stay order by Court of Civil Judge, Thane in  Regular Civil Suit case No. 251 of 2019 of Thane, on 25th day of June, 2019 due to which we were restrained from obtaining any permission for any further construction of the said Project or remaining part thereof till  01st day of July, 2020.

It was only on 23rd September, 2022, when the Hon’ble Supreme Court passed the order finalising the boundaries clarified that the Eco Sensitive Zone (ESZ) does not apply to Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) and the Thane Creek Flamingo Sanctuary.

4.	There was Change in planning as per Unified Development Control Regulation (UDCPR) applicable to whole Maharashtra except Mumbai due to which we were restrained from filing amended development permissions or business plans on 01st November, 2021. Finally on 6th April 2023 revised/amended development permissions were granted to the said Project by the Thane Municipal Corporation.

5.	Therefore, period commencing from 25th June 2019 till 6th April, 2023 i.e. 3 (Three) years 9 (Nine) months is to be specifically excluded from the completion time period due to the circumstances narrated hereinabove as per above mentioned . We have applied for Completion Certificate for, Wing A vide application dated 26/03/2018, Wing B to D vide application dated 08/02/2018 and Wing E vide application dated 26/09/2018 with Kulgaon Badlapur Municipal Council (KBMC). The project is under construction in three phases and are constructing huge 25 storied towers, whereby the project requires very skilled and expertise manpower and other engineering techniques. The multi storied towers of such size are being constructed for the first time in our city.
Our project being located in mofussil area i.e. extreme end of Ulhasnagar City adjoining Maharal Gaon, the quality of manpower and engineering required for such type of construction is not available in abundance. As you are aware that due to lack of supply of man power and resources we had applied for the extension for Phase III in past, which was duly sanctioned by your honor considering the difficulties faced by us.
Though we have utilized the available manpower and resources to the fullest of their potential for our Phase I & II, but still some work is pending due to shortage of the same. We are trying very hard to complete the Phase I & II on time but it seems difficult to complete the same on time, hence we need an extension of approx 6 months i.e. till 30/06/2019 to complete the both phases as we have planned.
We being in the real estate sector for 13 years have earned reputation and credibility from our customers and have never compromised in providing the quality service to our customers. For the sake of completing it on the above proposed date we cannot compromise in the quality of service and hence request you to grant us the revised date of completion as 30/06/2019 for our Phase I bearing Registration No. P51700002735 & Phase II bearing Registration No. P51700002911.

1)	The Applicant states that the project was delayed on account of various factors as below :

i.	There was non-availability of sand for the construction of the project as mining was banned in all Coastal Regulated areas across the State of Maharashtra.

ii.	The Quarrying for stones was simultaneously banned in the State by the Environment Ministry resulting into non-availability of stones on construction and which correspondingly caused delay in completion of the project. 

iii.	In view of the Hon’ble Bombay High Court in PIL No. 138 of 2006 on account of the ban, the stone Vendors were unable to provide the required quantity as well as quality of the stones which resulted in delay in construction progress.  

iv.	The ban Order by the Bombay High Court was finally lifted only in February, 2014 in view of the Orders passed by the Hon’ble National Green Tribunal.  

v.	The State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) would not give any clearance for any stone quarrying.

vi.	Serious economic downtown and down swing in the real estate industry, which also resulted in the balance flats not being sold, thereby affecting the cash flow;

vii.	Steep increase in price of stone, sand, steel, cement and other building materials and which the Applicant continued to procure inspite of sale of the premises was at a fixed price and no increase was demanded from the Allottees.

viii.	Interim Stay order dated 26th October 2016 passed by the Hon’ble State Commission on the sale of the adjacent plot which was to be sold so as to meet up with the escalated cost of construction and to complete the construction of 25 building. The stay was subsequently vacated vide the Disposal Orders passed by the Hon’ble State Commission on 27th February 2018 & Hon’ble NCRDC on 9th March 2018.

*	The Status of Construction of Building no. 1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10 are at final stage of Completion. Installation of lift is going on in building nos. 11,12,14,16 &17 and will be ready to handover for fit out Possession in the month of January 2020. The other facilities/amenities such as Electricity, Water connection, Fire Fighting, Solar Panel, Children’s Play area already functional. The Photographs of the same are annexed herewith as Annexure  A. 
*	The NBFC crisis has been a tip of the iceberg of the ongoing headwinds faced by the real estate industry with the slower receivable cycles and further stretched unreasonably causing developers to face the escalated heat of liquidity crisis on one side and managing delivery pressure under RERA on another side. However, the Developer with a sincere intent to deliver the project as committed, kept trying to arrange funds and tackle all the other hurdles. Looking at the recent market situation and NBFC crisis the Developer has time and again failed to arrange funds from the financial institutions. As because of the NBFC crises home loan disbursement was stopped and due to which installments were not received from the potential customer and thereby the cash-flow was affected.
*In due course of time we shall apply for OC (Occupancy Certificate).

extensions.reason: Work not Complete

The project was impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak in 2020 and 2021, and the subsequent slow market conditions and labour shortages made it difficult for us to complete the project on time. Therefore, we are requesting an extension of time within which the project shall be completed by the promoter to 31st December 2024.

The project is under constructoin but because of the following reasons we could not get the project finally completed:
1.	The promoter has suffered from financial difficulties due to adverse economic condition in the Indian Real Estate Market.
2.	The Parliamentary General election – 2024 & Maharashtra Assembly election - 2024 caused the halt to construction activities due to the absence of Staff.
3.	The promoter was not able to procure the skilled labour for the construction due to unfavourable labour market, whereby the labour migrated to their home state to exercise their electoral franchise.
4.	The promoter has suffered adverse climate condition at the construction site due to heavy rains of Mumbai costal causing water logging for weeks at the site.

extensions.reason:
The building named ‘FLORENCE’ was envisaged and designed to be a Ground + 24 storied structure with the total height of 76.5 mts. We had taken a commencement certificate and Fire N.O.C. till the Ground + 22nd floor. 
Further vide notification dated 16th January, 2018 the Thane Municipal Corporation (“TMC”) termed all Buildings above 70 mts. as ‘HIGH RISE’, amending it from an earlier cutoff of 90 mts. thereby making it mandatory for all the ongoing under construction projects and new constructions above 70 mts. to take clearance from the High Rise Committee (“HRC”).
Our projected height for 24 floors was 76.5 mts. and we had never envisaged that such a rule would come into existence. These rules were cumbersome for the ongoing constructions and many projects got stalled. To address this situation the Honorable Thane Municipal Commissioner issued new circular dated 3rd December, 2018 stating that existing ongoing or under construction projects would be given consideration and will be cleared on a case to case basis. However, necessary permissions from Chief Fire Officer (“CFO”) along with approval of a Structural Analysis Report and Geotechnical Analysis Report from panel members of Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute were made mandatory before a sanction could be granted.
 
We got the approval from the CFO, Thane in March 2019 for Ground + 24 floors (76.5 mts.) with an additional condition of putting sprinklers to each and every room. 
We received necessary approval from the ‘High Rise Committee’ on 18th January, 2020 a copy of which is enclosed for reference. 
This delay in receiving the approvals has been a major hurdle for us to complete work in time (i.e. March 2020) and since the building was already under construction we had no option but to wait for the requisite permissions in accordance with the new rules. Nevertheless, we are committed to delivering the project by December 2020 and hence we are seeking an extension for the same.

I/We the Promoters of the Project name Florence registered under project registration no P51700003627. We are thankful to the MahaRERA Authority for giving a six months extension because of Covid 19 to our project which was valid till 30th June 2021.
 
We would like to bring to your notice that our project is 70% completed. We have a total of 112 apartments, out of that 59 apartments are sold and 53 apartments are unsold which needs to be sold but without the Extension Number we are unable to sell those apartments. Hence we are making this application for Project Extension. We request you to grant extension for our project for One Year that is till 30th June 2022.

1)	After registration of the said Project with MahaRERA vide letter dated 05.03.2020 Thane Municipal Corporation has given stop work notice and had stopped further development of the said Project. 
2)	Subsequently, due to the spread of the Covid-19 Pandemic, lockdown was imposed in Thane by the Government of India and Government of Maharashtra from 24.03.2020. Due to prevalence of Covid-19 Pandemic the construction activity was reduced to standstill.
3)	The vicinity area of the said Project was declared as containment zone on many occasions by Thane Municipal Corporation, as residents of nearby vicinity of the said Project affected by Covid-19. 
4)	Unavailability of Labours and construction material has become major issues due to Covid-19 pandemic. In the circumstances the said Project was further delayed due to causes beyond the control of the Applicant.
5)	Government of Maharashtra made applicable Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations (UDCPR) for Thane City on 02.12.2020 and accordingly the Development Control Regulations of Thane Municipal Corporation ceased to operate. There were many ambiguities with respect to applicability of various provisions of UDCPR made applicable to the existing under construction projects, as it was transition period for the UDCPR from DCR of Thane Municipal Corporation.
6)	The applicant through its Architect 10 Fold Architects & Consultants has submitted application to Thane Municipal Corporation for further approval. The Thane Municipal Corporation has issued further Amended Commencement Certificate on 22.04.2022.
As per order of the Hon'ble Chairman (MahaRERA) Dated 12/12/2025 we request you kindly to grant us extension till 31/12/2027

At the time when we had applied for Occupancy Certificate, NMMC authorities has insisted for submission of Civil Aviation NOC. This Civil Aviation NOC was never a condition in our file since the project is located at the foothills of Parshik Hills which is higher in height than our proposed building. Hence we had obtained the CC in the year 2011 without the NOC. However, now on insistence of NMMC authorities we had applied for Civil Aviation NOC & our case has been referred to Delhi. The appellate authority is expected to review the case with 5-6 months. Till the time our case is been heard we have been granted Part Occupancy Certificate of the project. The same is uploaded on the website.

extensions.reason: We have changed the project from Residential cum Commercial project to Commercial Project for Sale Building which involved many changes in project implementation program and further covid outbreak has resulted in complete slow down in realty sector and more particularly for commercial project owing to emergence of WORK FROM HOME CONCEPT. We are very much sure and have taken into confidence majority of allottees while redesigning the project completion methodology. The total number of apartment includes rehab building also but number of apartment  for sale buildings are 138 and of which 63 apartment are sold and we have obtained consent from 45 apartment which comes to 71.43%. Hence the percentage reflected below should be ignored and it should be taken as 71.43%

The project was started prior to outbreak of COVID-19, which had an impact on real estate project for nearly 2 years, from March 2020 to February 2022 which has severely impacted the availability of labour and disrupted the supply chain, causing significant delays in the construction activities. This has resulted in slow progress in construction. However, we are trying to complete the project at the earliest. 
The cost of balance work to complete the construction is Rs. 1,78,48,08,892 /- which can be easily met out of receivable from sold units of Rs. 87,67,32,697/- and the fair value of unsold units of Rs. 1,38,99,96,715/- totalling to Rs. 2,26,67,29,412/-. The project can be completed with positive feasibility and cash flow. Refer to Form 2 as on 30/06/2025 certifying that balance work can be completed on or before 31/12/2026. Refer to Form 3 as on 30/06/2025 reflecting the financial feasibility for completion of the project.

The Project commenced under MMRDA Rental Housing Scheme whereby developers were offered additional FSI in return for providing tenements of 160 sq. ft. carpet area to MMRDA free of cost. The FSI of the free sale area is released in proportion to the construction of the rental housing units. In November 2016, demonetisation policy was announced which impacted the project. Material supply became irregular and unreliable. Labors rushed to their home town in panic resulting in almost complete halt of work at site. Due to the overall economic situation customers were avoiding making large purchases such as for flats and offices, which affected the entire real estate sector across the country including the said Project.  Due to this differences arose between the Promoter and PMC and accordingly in November 2017, PMC exited and Promoters appointed Big City Project Pvt. Ltd. as the new contractor. They conducted a survey to estimate the quantum of work to be completed and detailed discussion and negotiations took place for completing the balance work. This took time, due to the slump in the real estate market. Accordingly, the final agreement with Big City for completing the construction work as a Contractor was entered in November 2018. At present almost all civil work and 60% finishing work is complete. Promoter has substantially completed the project and will complete the remaining shortly. However, due to the aforesaid circumstances and to ensure the quality of the construction and as the earlier PMC exited there was a setback of approximately 12 months in the Project. It is in the best interest of the Project that the Promoter complete the Project hence, be granted an extension of 12 months for completing the said Project. The Promoter undertakes to complete the construction of the said Project within the extended period of time

extensions.reason: The project was impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak in 2020 and 2021, and the subsequent slow market conditions and labour shortages made it difficult for us to complete the project on time. Therefore, we are requesting an extension of time within which the project shall be completed by the promoter to 31st December 2024.

The project is under construction but because of the following reasons we could not get the project finally completed:
1.	The promoter has suffered from financial difficulties due to adverse economic condition in the Indian Real Estate Market.
2.	The Parliamentary General election – 2024 & Maharashtra Assembly election - 2024 caused the halt to construction activities due to the absence of Staff.
3.	The promoter was not able to procure the skilled labour for the construction due to unfavourable labour market, whereby the labour migrated to their home state to exercise their electoral franchise.
4.	The promoter has suffered adverse climate condition at the construction site due to heavy rains of Mumbai costal causing water logging for weeks at the site. 
Necessity for Extension:
The promoter requires the extension certificate for their prospective allottees, financial institutions of prospective allottees & for financial planning by the prospective allottees, as home finance companies require for the RERA certificate from the allottees.
The promoter requires the extension certificate to sell the unsold units of the project because it is statutory mandate for the promoter to have RERA certificate before executing any Agreement for Sale. 
The promoter requires the extension certificate to comply with the RERA Statutory requirements and for the compliance with Town Planning & Development laws.

We hereby request to your good office to grant the extension of proposed date of completion of project from 30th December 2024 to 30th June 2026.

Reasons for delay in completion of project are as follows:
i.	During the year 2023, monsoon season was extended till Noveber-2023, hence all the RCC work was delayed by 4 Months. The total cascading effect on the completion of RCC work is more than 6 months. The project alsofaced unexpected delays in obtaining various approvals and clearances from local authorities, resulting in a significant setback to the construction timeline.
ii.	M/s. Jaatvedas Construction Co. Pvt. Ltd. was appointed as our main civil contractor for the present project but they time and again defaulted in performing their obligations according to the agreed timeline, hence, delaying the project due to their defaults. There were disproportionate deployment of resources like manpower, material and plant and machinery. Soon, the contractor declared bankruptcy and as a result were not able to continue to complete the construction work any further. They applied for liquidation before the Company Law Tribunal and subsequently an IRP was appointed for the said contractor, which made it difficult to correspond. However, due to poor performance of contractor, they had been terminated and after which they raised false and frivolous claims against us and also filed a commercial suit against us before the Hon’ble Bombay High Court. A lot of time went in vain during the aforesaid litigation and legal compliances of court.
iii.	Aware from our previous experience and in order to finish the incomplete work at the redevelopment, we were very watchful in appointing another Civil Contractor after 2 months of hustle namely, M/s Astha Enterprises. Upon the restart of work by new contractor, it was observed by us in our supervision that the workmanship has been poor and there have been many safety issues at site, due to which the work had to be haulted. It was brought to our attention that the new contractors had carried out substandard quality of work at site and did not meet with the agreed timelines. A lot of time was lapsed in all these negotiations and meetings but considering regular inferior work done by the contractor, an arbitration proceeding was invoked against the contractor which is still pending till date.
iv.	There are also frequent and long term electricity failures at Thane, Panchpakhadi area. The government had banned the stone quarry in 2023, hence there was a negative impact on supply of concrete from RMC plant which severely hampered our construction timelines.

The construction work and finishing work of the buildings in the Project is totally completed and Flats are now in habitable condition. The Promoter is seeking Fire NOC and other NOCs from the concerned authorities so that file for issuance of Occupation Certificate (OC) can be uploaded. On receipt all such NOCs the Promoter shall immediately apply for the Occupation Certificate (OC) and on issuance of Occupation Certificate (OC) by the Thane Municipal Corporation the Promoter shall hand over the possession of respective Flats to the Allottees. This procedures may take approximate 6 months. Therefore, the 


Promoter need extension of 6 months to complete the project. Photographs of the building are enclosed herewith.

Further, we, M/s Metro Developers were also made a party to the said special suit. On February, 5, 2018, during the course of proceedings of the suit, the Honorable Court of Civil Justice, Kalyan, ordered all the parties to maintain ‘Status Quo’ in respect of any development or any activity over such land. On August 31, 2018, after extensive debate and representations on various dates, the Honorable Court decided the result in our favour and vacated the Status Quo. In a meanwhile, we lost 146 precious days (the period for which status quo was in place). We had to stop all construction and selling activities on and off the site till the status quo was in place. This has badly affected our construction work. Our contracts with suppliers of material, suppliers of labour and other agencies were put on hold or suspended or some had even been terminated due to uncertainty over the outcome of the litigation matter. Despite delay we have completed all construction activities and have applied to various government authorities for NoCs and final approvals. We expect to get all approvals within reasonable period of time and request to to kindly grant us the extension till June 30, 2019 to complete the project in all aspects. Detailed application is attached herewith. In case the authority needs any further information, documentation or explanation in this regard, an opportunity of being heard is requested.

extensions.reason: In accordance with circular no 28, we hereby apply for extension of our project u/s 6 in Format B. The project was delayed for reasons beyond our control on account of various reasons and more particularly on account of the pandemic of Covid-19.

The progress of the project slowed due to various reasons which overall impacted the timely completion of the Project, such as Covid 19 and contractor-related challenges, which affected the continuity of work. We faced operational setbacks due to labour shortages, and gaps in coordination among subcontractors. These issues affected adherence to planned schedules and slowed overall execution of the work.

Throughout this period, we continued to prioritize the interests of our allottees. We assure you that the delays were never due to negligence but due to circumstances beyond our immediate control.
We respectfully submit that we have always acted bona fide and in the best interests of the allottees. As a mark of our credibility and commitment, we state that we have successfully completed and delivered a real estate project named “Highland Park Building 6 And 7- K23 Phase 1” in the year 2019, thereby demonstrating our ability and intention to complete projects responsibly.

Further, despite the challenges faced, we have continued construction activity to the extent possible and have already handed over fit-out possession of 9 (nine) units to respective allottees.In view of the above facts and in the interest of justice, allottees, and orderly completion of the Project, we respectfully request the Hon’ble Authority to grant an extension of the Project completion date till 31/12/2026, in terms of MahaRERA Order No. 40.

1.The allottees of the project have already paid significant amount of consideration towards their respective flats in the project. To secure their funds and to deliver their flats, it is necessary to have the MahaRERA project registration extension certificate granted.
2.One of the major requirements for the allottees to register their agreement for sale and pay the stamp duty to the government is a valid MahaRERA Project Registration Certificate without which their agreement cannot be registered and the project cannot receive their payments which will lead to further delay and hardships to the project.
3.We have faced a challenging time during the past few years after COVID-19 and other force majeure events leading to the unprecedented delay in this project. However, we will ensure the delivery of the project with the help of a valid MahaRERA Project Registration Certificate. We have already taken stringent steps such as changing the primary contractor of the project and other project professionals to expedite the delivery of the project.

We apologize for the delay in the completion of the project. The construction was delayed mainly due to COVID, which severely impacted on the real estate sector. Medium-scale developers like Morya Infraconstruct Private Limited faced a liquidity crunch as flat sales remained stagnant for a long period and demand declined due to unemployment and recession.
Despite these challenges, we successfully completed Rehab Tower-1 (SRA building) and handed over possession to 130 tenants. The building plans were revised in January 2024, and approval for additional floors on both SRA towers was granted by SRA. Construction of SRA Tower-1 up to 17 floors is complete, the OC has been obtained, and tenants have been residing there since May 2024. Rehab Tower-2 construction is completed up to the 20th floor, with finishing work in progress. Possession will be handed over to tenants by May 2026. The sale tower was constructed up to the 19th floor, and finishing work is currently underway. Despite the setbacks, we are working diligently to address these issues and complete the remaining work.
Given the circumstances, we kindly request an extension until 31-12-2027, to complete the project and fulfil all regulatory requirements.

We may get an Occupation Certificate at any time within the applied extension period.   As per the provision u/s. 7(3) of RERA Act the society of the allottees in the said project has permitted us to take the extension period of time of six months and has passed the necessary resolution in respect thereof.

1.Pursuant to a Development Agreement, the Applicant alongwith the Society is a promotor of the project. Presently, the Applicant has completed construction of all G+27 Floors with all necessary amenities making the building habitable. The Applicant prays that the registration of the project be extended to 31.12.2019 in view of the following circumstances beyond the Applicant’s control: 
a.The Corporation (“TMC”) had sanctioned plans of G+27 floors. TMC issued a restricted Commencement Certificate (“CC”) dated 11.11.2014 for G+25 upper floors only. TMC issued further CC only on 04.12.2017. The aforesaid delay is attributable to pendency of the decision pertaining to Government Policy of Incentive FSI. The same is pending till date.
b.The Fire Department has granted Conditional NOC dated 26.08.2014. The aforesaid NOC was conditional upon removal of encroachments consisting of 17 Shops lying outside the project plot on adjoining tit bit land belonging to MHADA. The TMC’s encroachment department was liable to remove the encroachments which it failed to do. Thus the Applicant and the Society agreed that the Applicant would obtain the consent of the encroachers, new flat purchasers, TMC and MHADA and bear certain expenses to assist the Society to amalgamate the tit-bit land with the project plot to facilitate removal of the encroachers. The Society has accordingly passed a resolution dated 10.12.2018. Pursuant thereto the Applicant has completed all formalities expect execution of a Supplemental Agreement with the Society which is likely to be signed within 4 weeks on account of delay by the Society. Consent from 80% plus of new purchasers is also obtained. On execution of supplemental Agreement, Applicant can obtain necessary permissions to Demolish, reconstruct and rehabilitate the encroachers to obtain OC, which will take 11-12 months.
c.Pertinently, considering the aforesaid circumstances, no reliefs were granted against the Applicant in a complaint under Section 18.
